عَمِيدٌ : see عُمْدَةٌ ―
-b2- and see also عَمُودٌ, first quarter. ―
-b3- Also A man sick, (L,) or very sick, (A,) so that he cannot sit unless propped up by cushions placed at his sides. (A, * L.) ―
-b4- Also, and ↓ مَعْمُودٌ , (S, O, L, K,) and ↓ معَمَّدٌ , (K,) A man broken, or enervated, by the passion of love; (S, O, K;) and in like manner all the three are applied to a heart: (O:) or the first and second signify a man whose عَمُود of his heart is severed: (A:) or a man much distressed, or afflicted, by love; likened to a camel's hump of which the interior is broken: (L. [See عَمِدَ:]) and ↓ مَعْمُودٌ signifies diseased, or sick. (L.) ―
-b5- See also عَمُودٌ, last sentence. ＝
-A2- عَمِيدُ الوَجَعِ The place of pain. (L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
